Before the form and model of a commissarial act — in respect of the boundaries between the estates of His Sacred Royal Majesty on the one part and the hereditary terrestrial estates of the nobility on the other, erected or to be erected — is set forth, the difference, in particular how far royal commissions differ from the termination or delimitation of estates on both sides terrestrial, explained above, must first be considered; which may readily be gathered from the notes below.

And first, that for a future commissarial act, the referral of the land court to the field — which in the process described above, between estates on both sides terrestrial, is laid as its foundation — is not necessary; indeed, instead of the referral, a royal commission or instrument of commission must be obtained from His Sacred Royal Majesty, from the Chancery of the Kingdom, directed to certain ^[Five commissioners are to be present together with the Sub-Chamberlain.] principal persons — two of the dignitary order, two of the terrestrial officials, and a fifth of the Sub-Chamberlain or Boundary Chamberlain of whatever palatinate or land they may most readily be engaged — (who, on account of the absence of one or two, are customarily named in greater number) for the purpose of the delimitation of estates and the erection of mounds; which commission may also be issued outside the borders of the Kingdom, together
paciorkowski1776/83:
with a mandate to the leaseholders of the royal estates and to the collateral heirs.

And thereafter, in place of a summons, the summons letters ^[The summons letters and mandate must precede the session by two weeks.] of the lord commissioners, both to the Captain and to the collateral heir, for a certain fixed session and place, shall be issued and served by the court messenger and two noblemen two weeks before the session, together with the royal mandates; the service return of the same, once served, the same court messenger must acknowledge before the records of his own district; and the commissarial act itself must be concluded within the space of one year and six weeks.

Furthermore, that in the court and act of a commission, by virtue of the laws and constitutions of the Kingdom contained in this book, no postponement is granted, on the ground that it is an act of a single occasion; except that if the matter cannot be concluded in one day, it may be transferred to the next immediately following day and continued and executed on the morrow.

Moreover, no appeal from that commissarial court ^[In the commissarial act no postponement is granted. No appeal is granted.] and its decree lies to any higher court of the Kingdom, on the ground that it is an absolute court and has, by virtue of the laws of the Kingdom (its conscience alone obligated and burdened thereto), the absolute faculty and power of judging and distinguishing estates from royal ones.

Furthermore, as regards the form of this court: that ^[The royal subjects are required to confirm the mounds, not the leaseholder.] in respect of the right of path and the won boundary path, not the leaseholder of the royal estates but the peasant settlers of those same
paciorkowski1776/84:
estates, that is the village subjects, are required to confirm by oath the won boundary path regarding the true and just conduct and erection of the mounds at the very determination of the boundaries — namely six subjects from the community, in the oath formula prescribed by the statute of the Kingdom.

If, however, the heir of terrestrial estates wins the boundary path, then not his subjects but the nobleman himself, together with six witnesses of equal rank, shall be required to confirm the won boundary path in the oath formula prescribed by the statute of the Kingdom.

Moreover, when both parties are wanting in documentary proof ^[The commissioners make the boundaries in the absence of boundary markers.] and visible boundary markers, or only doubtful ones are standing, then in such a case, both parties' boundary paths having been rejected, the commissarial court shall determine the aforesaid boundaries from the thing presented to the eyes and by the moderation of its court, on equitable and just grounds, the oath barred to the parties.

^[Prosecutorial letters against the commissarial act are void and of no effect.] Furthermore, any citations and summonses to any court of the Kingdom whatsoever — whether on account of a motion or appeal not admitted, whether in accessory matters or in the final sentence, or for the purpose of quashing or relieving the commissarial act, issued on whatever legal pretext and ground — are void and of no effect, once the commissarial act has been determined in full and complete form, in the customary legal form and with all prior solemnities necessary for that purpose.

Furthermore, the penalty for the destruction of mounds
paciorkowski1776/85:
erected by the commissioners is far greater than for terrestrial ones, with restoration at the expense of the leaseholder of the royal estates, through the same number of commissioners and the Sub-Chamberlain's office designated by His Sacred Royal Majesty.

Finally, ^[Between royal and terrestrial estates no amicable settlement is granted.] whereas differences occasioned by the boundaries and limits between estates on both sides terrestrial may be resolved and settled by amicable composition, those between royal and terrestrial estates cannot be concluded and resolved by the same method and by amicable means, for the reason that they are estates of the Commonwealth, which cannot, without the consent of all the orders of the Kingdom, be alienated, nor in any part diminished, severed, or made to suffer detriment.

Commissarial Decree on Serious Contested Matters of the Parties, Issued by the Moderation of the Court.

Done at the field place of the differences between the estates of the village of [name], hereditary property of the Honourable [names], on the one part, and the estates of His Sacred Royal Majesty of the village of [name] belonging to the Captaincy of [name], presently leased to the Right Honourable [names], on the other part; beside a public road running from the town of [name] to the village of [name], and near three particular corner mounds or corner mounds — one of the aforesaid estates of the village of [name], the second of the estates of the village of [name]
paciorkowski1776/86:
of His Sacred Royal Majesty, and the third of the village of [name], hereditary property of the Honourable [names], collaterally summoned — situated on the border of the pine forest, at the place called [name]; on the Monday next after the feast of [names], in the year of the Lord [names].

Before the Illustrious Right Honourable [names], Castellan of [name], and the Right Honourable [names], Sub-Chamberlain of the Palatinate of [name] (the other several commissioners are to be given their proper titles, those who subscribed themselves upon the summons letters of the parties), commissioners designated and deputed by His Sacred Royal Majesty to decide, finally conclude, and determine the differences occasioned by the boundaries between the estates described above; by virtue of the Commission Letters issued under the title of His Sacred Royal Majesty, sealed with the seal of the greater or lesser Chancery of the Kingdom, sound, intact, and unimpaired, and bearing no mark of suspicion; ^[The Instrument of the Royal Commission of His Sacred Royal Majesty.] the tenor of which, word for word, follows and is as follows:

AUGUSTUS THE THIRD, by the Grace of God King of Poland, Grand Duke of Lithuania, Ruthenia, Prussia, Masovia, Samogitia, Livonia, Kiev, Volhynia, Podolia, Podlachia, Smolensk, Severia, and likewise Hereditary Duke of Saxony, Prince and Elector.

To the Right Honourable and Honourable [names] [names], sincerely and faithfully beloved by Us, Our royal grace. Right Honourable and Honourable, sincerely and faithfully beloved by Us: We have learned that differences have arisen on the occasion of the boundaries between Our royal estates of the town, namely
paciorkowski1776/87: of [name] and the villages belonging to it, leased to the Right Honourable [names], Palatine of [name], [names], Our Captain, on the one part; and the hereditary estates of the village of [name] of the Honourable [names], on the other part. Which matter We, desiring it to be settled and composed, have thought it fitting to commit to your Sincerity and Fidelity, in whose good faith, integrity, and skill in conducting affairs We have confidence and knowledge; as We commit it by these presents. Enjoining and commanding the same, that by mutually consulting together on a time and day suitable for that purpose, and fixing it among themselves, and having summoned the parties whose interest it concerns by their summons letters to their presence, they convene at the place of the differences; and there, having heard and listened to the submissions and responses of those same parties, and received the sufficient testimony of elderly witnesses of good repute, by means of their bodily oath if necessary, and having fully cognised and examined the thing itself presented to the eyes and the position and truth of that place — favouring neither party, but having only GOD and His justice before their eyes — let them delimit and distinguish the said estates, and mark them with mounds and metal markers, in the manner customary in such matters; being diligent, however, to provide that by this delimitation Our royal estates be in no way diminished. In which matter We burden the consciences of your Sincerity and Fidelity. Whatever, moreover, they shall enact and decree in that matter, We will to be ratified and acceptable, and
paciorkowski1776/88:
that it be kept and observed inviolably by the said parties. The absence of one or of several of your Sincerity and Fidelity notwithstanding, provided those are present and in such number as by law ought to be present. Given etc.

Those Commission Letters of His Sacred Royal Majesty having been read out, at today's session assigned to the parties by Us, or by our summons letters, as commissioners from His Sacred Royal Majesty, the commissarial jurisdiction having been founded and proclaimed with all security of the present act by the court messenger of the Kingdom, the Honest [name] of the village of [name], authentic and sworn, in the presence of the Honourable and Noble [names] and others of various rank and condition assembled for this act; the tenor of which summons letters issued to the Right Honourable Captain or leaseholder of the royal estates of the town of [name] and the villages belonging thereto, follows in this form: ^[Summons letters to the Right Honourable Captain from the commissioners.] We, [names] [names], commissioners designated and deputed by His Sacred Royal Majesty to perform the matters written below, give notice to you, the Right Honourable or Honourable [names], leaseholder or Captain of the royal estates of [name]: that the Commission Letters of His Sacred Royal Majesty have been presented to us, by which His Royal Majesty has seen fit to commit and command us to compose the differences occasioned by the boundaries between the above-named royal estates of [name], presently Your leaseholding, on the one part; and the hereditary estates of the village of [name] of the Honourable [names],
paciorkowski1776/89: on the other part; to distinguish them by mounds and metal markers and others customarily done in such matters, except that first the sufficient testimony of elderly witnesses of good repute shall be received, by their bodily oath if necessary; and to mark and delimit them — of the Commission Letters themselves, of which fuller account will be given to You at the approaching session, in their tenor. Wherefore We command You and the community of the subjects of the aforesaid village of [name], by royal authority and Our own commissarial authority which We exercise in this matter, that You and the true community of the subjects, with Your assistance as leaseholder, appear personally, legitimately, and peremptorily before Us and Our commissarial court, on the [day] next after the feast of [name], next and immediately to come, at the aforesaid place of the differences, where We shall have been situated and stationed by the plaintiff's party, at the instance of the aforesaid Honourable [names], heir of the village of [name], plaintiff; and that You judicially attempt the matter of the delimitation of the aforesaid estates, and respond to whatever by law shall be due. Certifying You that whether You appear or not at the fixed session, We shall nonetheless proceed to those matters that are incumbent upon Us from the prescription of the laws. Your contumacy and that of the subjects of the aforesaid royal estates subject to Your possession, and Your opposition, notwithstanding. Given at Our places of residence on the [day] next, in the year of the Lord [names].
paciorkowski1776/90:
^[Royal mandate to the Right Honourable Captain.] The series of the Royal Mandate of His Sacred Royal Majesty given to the same Right Honourable Captain is as follows: AUGUSTUS THE THIRD, by the Grace of God King of Poland, Grand Duke of Lithuania, Ruthenia, Prussia, Masovia, Samogitia, Kiev, Volhynia, Podolia, Podlachia, Livonia, Smolensk, Severia, and Chernigov, and likewise Hereditary Duke of Saxony, Prince and Elector.

To the Right Honourable or Honourable [names] [names], Captain or leaseholder of Our estates, sincerely and faithfully beloved by Us. We have designated certain of Our commissioners to make and establish boundaries between Our royal estates of the town or village of [name] of the leaseholding of Your Fidelity on the one part, and the hereditary estates of the village of [name] of the Honourable or Noble [name] on the other part. Wherefore We require Your Fidelity, that as soon as it shall have been summoned by the summons letters of the aforesaid Our commissioners, it appear before them at the aforesaid place of the differences, be present at the delimitation of the estates, and keep and observe firmly whatever they shall decree in that matter. Let it take care, however, that no detriment be done to Our royal estates by that delimitation. For Our grace. Given etc. The service return of which mandate, acknowledged for service in the estates of [name] before the municipal records of [name] on the [day] of [name] in the year of the Lord [names], by the court messenger of the Kingdom, the Honest [names] of the village of [name], together with two noblemen [names].
paciorkowski1776/91: Thereafter were issued the summons letters of the Right Honourable Commissioners [names] against the Honourable [name], heir of the estates of the village of [name], collateral heir; the acknowledged service return of those same served letters by the same court messenger, before the municipal records of [name], together with the mandate of His Sacred Royal Majesty; ^[Summons letters to the Honourable collateral heir.] the tenor of which follows in this form: Done at the castle of [name], on the [day] of [name] in the year [name] etc. (Written from the authentic extract of the service return.) We etc., commissioners designated and deputed by His Sacred Royal Majesty to perform the matters written below. To you, the Honourable [names], heir of the estates of the village of [name], collateral heir: we give notice that the Commission Letters of His Sacred Royal Majesty have been presented to us, by which His Majesty has seen fit to commit and command us to compose the differences occasioned by the boundaries between the royal estates of [name] of the leaseholding of the Right Honourable [names], Captain of [name], on the one part, and the hereditary estates of the village of [name] of the Honourable [name], plaintiff, on the other part; to distinguish them by mounds and metal markers customarily used in such matters, and to mark and delimit them. Since, however, your aforesaid estates of [name] are said to lie contiguous to the estates principally to be delimited: we therefore command You, by royal authority and Our commissarial authority which We exercise in this matter, that You appear personally and peremptorily before Us and Our commissarial court, on the [day] next after the feast of [name], next and immediately to come, at the aforesaid place of the differences, where We shall have been situated and
paciorkowski1776/92:
stationed by the aforesaid plaintiff's party, at the instance of the above-named heir [name], plaintiff; and that You judicially attempt this matter of the delimitation of the aforesaid estates, and acknowledge Your boundary wall from Your hereditary estates of the village of [name] and Your corner point or particular corner point existing at the convergence of three estates, and respond to whatever by law shall be due. Certifying You that whether You appear at the fixed session or not, We shall nonetheless proceed to those matters that are incumbent upon Us from Our office and the prescription of the laws, against You — Your absence, contumacy, and unlawful opposition notwithstanding. Given at Our place of residence on the [day] etc.

Likewise the Royal Mandate of His Sacred Royal Majesty given to the same cited collateral heir of the village of [name], of the following tenor: AUGUSTUS THE THIRD etc. The title shall be written from the foregoing act.

To the Honourable [names], heir of the estates of the village of [name], faithfully beloved by Us. Honourable, faithfully beloved by Us. We have designated certain of Our commissioners to make boundaries between Our royal estates of the town of [name] and the villages belonging to it, presently leased to the Right Honourable or Honourable [names] and [name], Noble [names], and his hereditary estates on the other part. Since, however, the above-named hereditary estates of [name] of Your Fidelity are said to lie adjacent to those same estates to be delimited, We therefore command Your Fidelity
paciorkowski1776/93:
that as soon as You shall have been summoned by the summons letters of the aforesaid Our commissioners, You appear before them at the place of the differences, attempt the boundary wall of Your estates, and where it is to be acknowledged, acknowledge it. Whatever, moreover, they shall decree in that matter, keep and observe it firmly and inviolably. For Our grace. Given at Warsaw etc. (It is to be noted that if there are several collateral heirs on the other boundary of the boundary wall, they are likewise to be summoned by summons letters and mandate.)

After which enrolment, the commissarial court caused the parties to be called to appear. Those having been called, the Honourable [names], heir of the estates of the village of [name], personally arriving at that place, ^[The collateral heir protests, not acknowledging for the plaintiff the convergence of three estates and the corner point at that place.] not acknowledging there the true convergence of three estates, but elsewhere, where he offers to demonstrate it; and the mounds which the plaintiff's party takes as corner mounds for itself are not true mounds but hillocks — and on that account reproduced before his commissarial court the boundaries or official act drawn from the Sub-Chamberlain's records of [name], of the act of [name] in the year [name], from which it appears that the corner point or particular corner point of those estates existed in another place, and on that account protested against the same Honourable [names], plaintiff, regarding the improper founding of his court, as being on his own property, subject to no dispute, proceeding only to the avulsion of the hereditary estate of the protestant
paciorkowski1776/94: ^[The plaintiff counter-protests regarding the improper repulsion.] The Honourable [names], plaintiff, counter-protested against the Honourable [name] regarding his improper repulsion of both the plaintiff himself and the commissarial court from the place of the founded jurisdiction, alleging that the boundary act which the collateral party produces does not bear upon this place of the founded jurisdiction at all, but upon another corner point and boundary wall of that same hereditary village; regarding which improper demonstration he solemnly protested. ^[The Captain likewise protests, not acknowledging the corner point at the place of the founded jurisdiction.] The Right Honourable Captain likewise protests, not acknowledging at the place of the founded jurisdiction the true corner point, nor the convergence of the three aforesaid estates, but elsewhere, where he offers and declares he will demonstrate it in his boundary path. Having noted the protests and counter-protests of the parties, he orders the registration of appearance for those same parties. The plaintiff's party with ^[Appearance.] the Honourable [names] in person; the Right Honourable [names], Captain of [name], and the Honest [names], advocate, and the whole community of the settlers of the aforesaid royal village, cited, in the assistance of their master, in person; the Honourable [names], heir of the collateral estates of the village of [name], likewise in person; appearing before his court and judicially contesting the matter between themselves. The Royal commissarial court of His Sacred Royal Majesty, finding the appearance of the parties sufficient, orders those same parties to proceed to trial in the present case. In the trial, the contested submissions having been heard and
paciorkowski1776/95: weighed carefully and diligently; the decision of the corner point or particular corner point ^[The decision of the corner point duly suspended.] of the aforesaid estates being suspended — as not having been acknowledged, indeed denied, both by the Honourable [names], collateral heir, and by the Right Honourable Captain — ^[The court proceeded to the review of the boundary paths.] the court proceeded to the review of the boundary paths to be demonstrated by the parties. The sun at last declining toward the west, he ordered the commissarial act to be adjourned to the morrow by the court messenger of the Kingdom, the Honest [names], apparitor of his court. The morrow arriving, namely the Tuesday after the feast of [names] in the present year, the commissarial jurisdiction having been reassumed and proclaimed by the aforesaid court messenger, he proceeded to the review of the plaintiff's party's boundary path first, and declared that it should follow the same. And first the plaintiff's party commenced its boundary path ^[The plaintiff's party's boundary path.] from the place of the founded jurisdiction and from those same three corner mounds, from the west toward the east, as straight as possible; and demonstrated to the court a hillock resembling a mound, fifty paces from the corner mounds, at the edge of a dense pine forest grown with various kinds of trees; against which demonstration of the mound, both the Right Honourable Captain and his subjects protested, denying it to be a true mound but a hillock built by ants; and in verification thereof requested its opening, granting which application as allowable by law,
paciorkowski1776/96: in which, when opened, nothing was found save ants mixed with earth. Proceeding further toward the same eastern quarter, through that same pine forest, the court reached a place called Czarny Smug, at which place it demonstrated to the court a hillock in the manner of a mound, having no circle or roundness; in which, when opened at the application of the party, nothing was found. Continuing its boundary path further toward the same quarter, and crossing with difficulty the boggy and waterlogged places called Białe Ługi, it demonstrated to the court, in a more elevated place, an oblong hillock, not resembling a mound at all; and likewise, when the same was opened, no metal markers were found. And proceeding further through the same pine forest with the path cleared, curving and not in a straight line toward the winter east, inclining this way and that, it demonstrated to the court a hillock of no small height, taking it as a wall mound; regarding which demonstration the Right Honourable Captain protested regarding the unlawful display, asserting that it had grown from the roots of a felled tree; the party having requested the opening, the roots of the felled tree and part of a rotted trunk were found therein. Continuing its boundary path further and inclining toward the southern quarter, the court reached a small river flowing from the mill of [name] of the village of [name]; which small river the plaintiff's party took as the boundary wall and natural boundary, and proceeding along that same small river
paciorkowski1776/97: for almost one quarter of a mile, and thereafter leaving it and proceeding through dry scrubland for three or four furlongs, it demonstrated to the court a ditch dug by human hand, alleging it to be a boundary ditch representing the boundary wall; at which place the Right Honourable Captain protested against the aforesaid Honourable [names] regarding the unlawful conduct of the commissarial court and the illegal demonstration of the boundary path, alleging that the small river flowing from the Captain's mill is not the natural boundary of the aforesaid estates, since both its banks and bed are the proper property of the royal estates and belong to the village of [name]; and likewise that the ditch is not a boundary ditch, but has been erected only around a clay deposit, at present grown over with scrub. That ditch extending for only one furlong, the court reached a place called Ostra Górka, at which it demonstrated particular corner mounds or corner mounds, concluding and determining the boundary wall of its estate and of the royal estates of the village of [name]; and beside the particular corner mound of the collateral heir, the Honourable [names], heir of the estates of the village of [name], determined its boundary path. Against that entire boundary path the same Right Honourable Captain protested ^[The Captain protests against the entire boundary path of the plaintiff's party.] — regarding its nullity as containing the greatest obliqueness, first toward the east and then toward the south, inclining this way and that in a curve, conducted partly through the proper plots of the royal estates of the estate
paciorkowski1776/98: ^[Determination of the plaintiff's party's boundary path.] of the village of [name], partly with the small river taken wall-fashion as a natural boundary, confirmed by no documents and demonstrated by no real mounds. The Honourable [names] counter-protests against the aforesaid protest, having duly and legitimately continued his boundary path, and offers and declares that he will prove the same both by documents in the course of the case and by sworn inquiries. At which place the same plaintiff's party requested of the court of the Illustrious and Right Honourable Commissioners that the Honourable [names], heir of the village of [name], as the final collateral heir of the determined boundary path, be called to the court, pursuant to the commissarial summons letters issued at his instance against the same, of the following tenor: (Similar and conforming summons letters as against the first collateral heir at the commencement of the boundary path shall be inserted, with the name and surname and estates changed, and likewise by virtue of the royal mandate directed to that same cited heir for that purpose; a similar mandate as above.) To which application the Illustrious and Right Honourable Commissioners ordered the aforesaid Honourable [names], heir of the village of [name], as the final collateral heir, to be called to their court; ^[Acknowledgement of the corner point or particular corner point by the final collateral heir.] who, called by the aforesaid court messenger, appeared in person at that place, and there at that same place called Ostra Górka, acknowledged the convergence of the boundary walls of three estates, or the true particular corner point, of the village of [name], hereditary property of the Honourable plaintiff, and of the village of [name] of the royal estates, and of his own third collateral estate;
paciorkowski1776/99:
and proved it by the boundaries of the year [names].

The plaintiff's boundary path having been reviewed and faithfully noted by the commissarial court, it proceeded to the review of the Right Honourable Captain's boundary path. And ^[The Right Honourable Captain's boundary path.] first he commenced his boundary path from this corner point or particular corner point, acknowledged by the Honourable [names], collateral heir, and proceeded toward the north from the south, and reached a oak forest called Dąbrowa, and there beside a road not much frequented running from the village of [name] to the village of [name], demonstrated to the court a hillock, alleging it to be the first wall mound, almost three furlongs from that same corner point; the plaintiff's party requested its opening; in which, when opened, nothing was found save what appears to be mixed earth. From that mound, proceeding in a straight line through that same oak forest, he reached transverse roads — one running from the town of [name] to the village of [name], the other from the village of [name] to the village of [name] — between which roads he showed the court a hillock in the manner of a mound; in which, when opened, nothing was found. Proceeding further along the boundary path from that opened, allegedly mound, inclining toward the midpoint between the east and the north, he led the court to the boggy and waterlogged place Białe Ługi, and crossing the boundary of that same place, demonstrated to the court an incision in a birch tree in the manner of a cross; and from that tree proceeding toward the north through a forest grown partly
paciorkowski1776/100:
of pine, partly of oak, partly of hazel, for almost six furlongs from that birch tree, demonstrated to the court a similar incision in a maple tree, alleging those incisions as marking the boundary wall. The Honourable [names], plaintiff, protested against the unlawful demonstration by the Right Honourable Captain and his subjects — both of the hillocks and of the incisions freshly made not long ago by his subjects; regarding which unlawful act, he produced a protest and an inspection by the court messenger together with noblemen [names] of those same incisions, before the municipal records of [name] in the year [name], and proves it at the present session.

The Right Honourable Captain counter-protesting that those same incisions were made from antiquity, and the mounds are truly real, because antiquity was not in the habit of placing metal markers. Having thus noted the protests, he led the court to the boundary of that same forest, and beneath the very forest, toward the fields and plots of the estate of the village of [name], at the convergence of three estates, ^[Determination of the Right Honourable Captain's boundary path.] with the collaterally summoned party present and acknowledging the same, determined his boundary path. The plaintiff's party protests the nullity and invalidity of the entire boundary path, as having been conducted obliquely, neither through the intermediate points nor to the end point.

Both boundary paths of the parties having thus been concluded and reviewed, he limits the present act as the sun declines toward the west, to the morrow, and orders the court messenger
paciorkowski1776/101: to adjourn the same. The morrow arriving, namely the [day] of [name] in the year [name], the jurisdiction having been reassumed from the abovementioned limiting incident, ^[In the prosecution.] he ordered the parties to proceed in the case. In the prosecution of the case, he finds ^[A sworn inquiry enjoined.] that a sworn inquiry is necessary for more sufficient proof of the boundary paths; decreeing that both parties, and likewise the collateral heir, the Honourable [names], standing in the position of an uncertain corner point — and indeed the principal acting parties in respect both of the corner point and of the general boundary path; and the Honourable [names], collateral heir, as regards his corner point or particular corner point only, where the true convergence of three estates may be found — shall conduct that sworn inquiry and call witnesses, with prior interrogatories drawn up and communicated to one another, and this immediately; and the court messenger is added for the pronouncing of the oath formula regarding the impartiality of the witnesses. Which oath, since the parties — both the principal acting parties and the collateral heir — before the face of his court, before the image of the Crucified Lord, with the court messenger reading the formula to them, swore; he therefore proceeded to conduct that same sworn inquiry, and orders the parties to call witnesses — first for the plaintiff's party and then for the cited party. They called, produced, and swore. The sworn inquiries having been produced and concluded, he descended to the reading thereof. Which having been read and weighed and examined in all their circumstances with the mature deliberation
paciorkowski1776/102: of his court — since both ^[Final decree.] parties are wanting in their proofs — the court, resolving the suspension of the cognisance of the corner point or particular corner point of the principal acting parties' estates and of the Honourable [names], collateral heir, made previously: both those same parties' boundary paths having been rejected as proved by no documentary evidence or sworn inquiries — save that in the one and only corner point both parties and the collateral heir acknowledged to one another the convergence of three estates; whereas in the boundary paths one party had continued obliquely into the other's proper plots, demonstrated hillocks to the court in place of mounds, and conducted its boundary paths through almost all four quarters of the compass, starting from the north and going first toward the east, then toward the south and west — the commissarial court, for the reasons alleged above, from the thing presented to the eyes and in part from the sworn testimonies of elderly witnesses, favouring neither party and having only GOD and its conscience before its eyes, declares that it directs the boundary path at the arbitration of its court and erects the mounds (the oath barred, so that perjuries may not occur on the part of either party); and assigns the place called [names] for the corner mounds of those same aforesaid estates, and the court proceeded to the erection of mounds — first the corner mounds at that same assigned place; and indeed first for the plaintiff's party and its estate a corner mound was raised toward the east,
paciorkowski1776/103: for the royal estates toward the west, and for the Honourable [names], collateral heir, and his estate of the village of [name] toward the north; with the placing of metal markers in each of them, namely charcoal, brick, and iron slag, and glass bottles filled with millet, with a description in parchment of the present act by which the delimitation of those estates is made, with the year and act, so that it may remain for posterity in the event of any question arising. And from that same corner point, toward the south a first wall mound was raised, eighty paces from the corner point; (and so the boundary path and the erection of the mounds shall be written out and accurately described, so that the description thereof corresponds with the position of the places); and the court reached the particular corner mounds or corner mounds situated in the southern quarter, pursuant to the acknowledgement of the collateral heir, and ordered those same mounds to be renewed with the placing of metal markers, as placed at the original corner point. The boundaries having been duly and legitimately determined, the Illustrious and Right Honourable Commissioners by their authority order the parties to keep those same boundaries and observe them inviolably, and will and declare that they shall have the force of perpetual and inviolable validity; and decree in the present that whatever is on the right side of the hereditary estates from the original corner point to the determination of the particular corner point shall belong entirely to the estate of the village of [name].
paciorkowski1776/104:
Terrestrial estate; and whatever is on the left side and left hand, similarly entirely, shall for all time belong and pertain to the aforesaid estates of the village of [name] of His Sacred Royal Majesty; this also being provided and safeguarded: that the heirs and leaseholders of the aforesaid estates now delimited shall not deny one another mutual pasture in their respective estates (being careful, however, of damage), but shall maintain it among themselves, and their successors for all perpetual times. Which the above-named court messenger was ordered to proclaim and announce, by virtue of the present decree.

Commissarial Decree on Serious Contested Matters of the Parties, with the Oath Enjoined upon the Party That Has Won the Boundary Path.

paciorkowski1776/116:
On Royal Commissions and Commissioners, for the Delimitation of Royal and Terrestrial Estates.

Formerly two dignitaries and a Sub-Chamberlain were given for commissions on boundaries.

But henceforth five commissioners shall be appointed.

^[Herburt, fol. 95.] Likewise, since injuries and oppressions, and sometimes even acts of killing, were committed between Our registered and unregistered estates and those of Our neighbouring subjects; and since many difficulties arose in the delimitation of the boundaries, with Our Captains or leaseholders oppressing Our neighbouring subjects under cover of Our royal name and Our estates, or obstructing the delimitation of the boundaries — therefore, from the virtue and royal benevolence innate in Us, for the sake of all justice and peace for Our subjects in this matter, We promise: that to all Our subjects of whatever rank and condition, seeking boundaries from the side of Our estates, We and Our successors, according to the ancient statutes, for the discernment of equity, shall appoint and shall cause to be appointed the commissioners of that land and district in which the estates to be delimited are situated,
paciorkowski1776/117:
namely two dignitaries and two officials, together with the Boundary Chamberlain thereof.

The commissioners, having received an oath from the elderly witnesses on both sides, shall make the delimitation.

^[Herburt, ibid.] Which commissioners, after they have gone out, must summon the elderly witnesses from both sides; from whom, having received an oath, they shall proceed to the delimitation according to their recognition and testimony. If, however, those same elderly witnesses are in disagreement, then the commissioners according to their consciences, reconciling the disagreements of the elderly witnesses according to their own private judgment, shall pursue and conclude the delimitation itself. Where, moreover, the commissioners themselves should disagree, We will that the defined authority and power to conclude shall rest with the sentence of those who are in agreement by a majority of voices — the opposition of Our officials, namely the Captain or leaseholder, notwithstanding.

If commissioners are lacking in the proper district.

^[Herburt, ibid.] If, however, there were few dignitaries in that land or palatinate in which the boundaries are to be made who could be designated for those boundaries, or if they happened to be absent — in that case, from a neighbouring palatinate, or even from a more distant one,
paciorkowski1776/118:
We shall designate commissioners for the making of those same boundaries; none, however, other than those who shall have possessions in those lands where the boundaries are to be made.

The Captains shall defend the royal estates until the delimitation.

^[Herburt, fol. 49.] We enact: that henceforth the Prefects of Our castles and cities shall not obtain commissions for the fixing of boundaries, but noblemen alone; ^[A nobleman who obstructs a commission shall be liable.] yet so that nevertheless it shall be lawful for Our Prefects or Captains (as has been received by ancient custom and is provided by statute) to defend Our estates until the declaration of the boundaries.

The Captain or leaseholder of the royal estates shall go out to the delimitation of the estates, and shall provide for the commissioners if he holds free estates.

^[Herburt, fol. 96.] We shall command Our Captain or leaseholder of Our estates to go out and descend together with those same commissioners to delimit those same estates, and to provide for the commissioners at his expense — in particular with respect to those estates which We hold free and without encumbrance.

The session of the commission for delimiting the estates: two weeks.

^[Herburt, ibid.] The commissarial summons together with the mandate
paciorkowski1776/119:
to the Captain must be served by the court messenger and two noblemen two weeks before the delimitation, so as to certify the Captain both as to the time and as to the place.

Moreover, Our aforesaid commissioners, two weeks before they convene together for the making of the boundaries, shall inform Our Captain or leaseholder ^[The mandate shall be served in the presence of two noblemen.] of the time and place of their convening through the court messenger and two noblemen, and also through their own letters and Our mandate.

On the honour and security of the commissioners.

^[Herburt, ibid.] If any commoner, in the matter and court of the boundaries, ^[A violator of the commissarial act shall be referred to the Captain of that place for due penalties.] or on any other occasion, should inveigh against the commissioners in words and dishonour them — such a person shall be punished with imprisonment, or otherwise with a sitting of half a year. The execution of that penalty the Captain of that place shall carry out, under the penalty prescribed in the statute against those who should neglect to carry out its execution. Should any person, even a commoner, seize and brandish arms — even if he wounded no one — he shall pay the penalty with his neck; which the Captain shall likewise execute. Nobility, however, for such excesses shall be punished according to the statute.
paciorkowski1776/120:
What has once been decreed by the commissioners in the delimitation of estates shall not be renewed.

^[Herburt, ibid.] In order that what has once been decreed by Our commissioners (which We grant with respect to the delimitation of Our royal and noble estates) shall no longer be renewed, We enact: that after the delimitation of Our royal and noble estates, Our Captains shall do no injury in the plots of the nobility; and Our subjects shall have no usufruct in the delimited plots, neither bee-keeping nor any other advantage.

Whatever the commissioners shall have done shall stand. No reviewers shall be appointed.

^[Herburt, fol. 97.] We shall appoint Our commissioners to make the boundaries; and their judgment We shall not obstruct by Our inhibitions; We shall designate neither assessors nor commissioners, nor a reviewer, after the boundaries have been made. But whatever Our Commissioners ^[Commissioners shall make the boundaries between the royal estates notwithstanding the contumacy and opposition of the possessor.] shall have decreed, that shall be ratified and firm. Moreover, when Our commissioners convene at the place of the boundaries — whether Our Captain or leaseholder has gone out or not, whether he has produced the elderly witnesses or not — the commissioners themselves shall nonetheless pursue and conclude those same boundaries: the opposition and likewise the absence of Our Captains, and of those who seek remedy on account of injuries to the boundaries by way of motion and appeal,
paciorkowski1776/121:
notwithstanding in the slightest.

On commissioners unjustly cited, and on other courts.

^[Herburt, ibid.] Whoever should cite the commissioners, or any court or office, on account of any process — and such person shall be determined to have cited them unjustly — shall be required to give twenty-eight marks to each separately as a penalty. Likewise to the party, if the same should be cited.

Letters of the commissioners issued for the delimitation need no confirmation.

^[Herburt, fol. 271.] Induced by the petitions of Our subjects, We permit: that it shall be in the discretion of Our subjects to petition and obtain from Us a confirmation of the letters of boundaries issued by five commissioners ^[A completed commissarial act requires no approval.] deputed by Us according to the tenor of the statute. Which letters, in which Our commission and mandate shall have been inserted and the seals of the commissioners affixed, shall obtain authority and perpetual force, even if no confirmation of Ours intervenes thereupon.
paciorkowski1776/122:
How royal estates that have not been delimited are to be defended, and how Captains are to be proceeded against in law for injuries.

^[Herburt, fol. 48.] Likewise We enact: that leaseholders of the estates of Our Royal Table, ^[The land court is assigned as the forum for the Captain in matters of boundaries.] if they suffer injury from neighbours or others, shall be required to stand before the land court, after they have been summoned on account of the injury suffered. Even if they drive cattle or livestock to royal lordships or courts on account of a difference of boundaries, or on account of the destruction of crops — they shall be required to give to suretyship for a decree of the lords, according to the custom of the land long observed. If they do otherwise, they shall pay penalties like other nobles; which penalties may be sought and exacted from them, even in money, if any they shall have inscribed in the royal estates.

The boundaries of estates, metal markers, the testimony of elderly witnesses, and other possible evidences, make boundaries.

^[Herburt, fol. 267.] Moreover, for the removal of difficulties in the making of boundaries, We enact: that Our commissioners, having only GOD before their eyes and favouring neither party, having first examined the metal markers and diligently investigated the truth of the matter — both from the testimony of elderly witnesses, sworn if necessary, and from other possible indications — shall establish the boundaries between Our royal
paciorkowski1776/123:
and hereditary estates according to their arbitration and conscience.

When the boundaries have been made, the Captains shall not commit injury.

^[Herburt, ibid.] So that what is defined once by Our commissioners appointed for the delimitation of Our royal and noble estates may no longer be called into dispute: We enact that after the delimitation of Our royal and noble estates, Our Captains or officials shall not commit injury in the noble plots. And Our subjects too shall have no use of such delimited plots — neither in bee-keeping nor on any account.

 

The boundaries erected by the commissioners are to be kept for ever by the Starostas.

^[Constitution 1550, fol. 598.] So that what has once been made by Our commissioners, whom We appoint for the delimitation of Our royal estates and those of the nobility, shall never be renewed: We enact that after the delimitation of Our royal estates and those of the nobility, Our Starostas or officials shall not
paciorkowski1776/124:
commit injuries in the noble plots. And Our subjects shall have no use of such delimited plots — neither in bee-keeping nor in any manner. Constitution 1550, fol. 598. Załuski.

We leave in force the statute concerning the erection of boundaries between Our estate and the terrestrial estates.

^[Constitution 1562, fol. 621, vol. 2.] And any Starosta who destroys the boundaries: he shall be required to erect them again by the feast of Saint JOHN the Baptist next to come, under pain of deprivation of the office of the Captaincy or of the leasehold of the castle; and they shall be kept firmly with mounds in perpetuity. And where anyone should be summoned in respect of them at the instance of the Instigator of Our office from the denunciation of the Captain or leaseholder, We exempt all persons from such summonses.

On boundaries in the Duchy of Masovia.

^[Constitution 1569, fol. 790, vol. 2.] Boundaries in the Duchy of Masovia, made by commissioners appointed by Us between Our plots and those of the nobility, lawfully — that is, where Our mandate with the commissarial summons, issued in time according to the statute dealing with this matter, has been or shall in the future be issued to the Starosta or leaseholder of Our estates;
paciorkowski1776/125:
and which shall in the future be made, even where Our steward was not present at their making, who in respect of such boundaries has and can have no interest in the future according to the law and ancient observance — all shall be firmly kept by the Starostas and leaseholders of Our estates and by Our subjects for ever; which We confirm by this constitution, and according to the old laws of the Crown, according to which also in Masovia commissioners are and shall be appointed, the confirmations of those commissioners shall be issued from Our Chancery, to whoever shall have need of it. And those noblemen who are summoned on behalf of the Starostas in the name of Our Instigator, for any injuries or losses that might be contained within those boundaries — all of them We exempt from such summonses.

On destroyed boundaries.

^[Constitution 1578, fol. 977, vol. 2.] Boundaries that have been juridically concluded by Our commissioners between Our estates and those of the nobility — let neither Our Starostas and leaseholders nor the subjects in Our estates dare to violate or destroy them. And if any have been destroyed since the constitution of the year one thousand five hundred and sixty-two, they shall erect them again at their own expense through the commissioners, before the feast of Saint JOHN the Baptist next to come, having paid the party one hundred marks
paciorkowski1776/126:
as a fine, as often as they shall be summoned. And if Our subjects — namely commoners — should obstinately, without the command of the Starosta or Our leaseholder, destroy such boundaries — they shall be punished by a fine of fifty marks, as often as they shall be summoned; notwithstanding, the Starosta or leaseholder shall at their expense bring out the commissioners for the repair of the destroyed boundaries, at the latest within twelve weeks of their destruction.

On royal commissions and commissioners for boundaries.

^[Constitution 1588, fol. 1210, vol. 2.] Royal commissions for boundaries shall always be given from Our Chancery without any difficulty to whoever has need of them. And the commissioners, together with the Sub-Chamberlain or Boundary Chamberlain of that land, may be appointed not only from that but also from another closer palatinate, even if they have no residence in that palatinate or land. Which commissioners, when they subscribe themselves upon the summons letters, are required to arrive at the session and bring that commission to execution by making the boundaries. And if they cannot be concluded in one day, they are to conclude them on the following days without departing, so that the commission shall not lapse for the nobleman. And where a commissioner, having subscribed himself upon the summons letters, should fail to arrive at the session, he forfeits to the party one hundred marks, for which the forum shall be before the Tribunal, excepting true
paciorkowski1776/127: illness, which according to the law he is required to swear. The Starosta, like the nobleman, shall have no more of a retinue than thirty persons with friends and servants; and subjects at most twenty, for the showing of markers and the erection of mounds. And so that perjuries may not occur with offence to GOD, the commissioners are first to examine the markers shown from both sides by an elderly witness, and consider the matter among themselves according to their conscience; and if either party should show legitimate markers and probabilities: they shall require that party to prove it through elderly witnesses. And if both sides show uncertain markers, then without taking oaths from both sides, on account of the risk of perjury, they are to make the boundaries according to their conscience, inclining toward the statute and juxta æquitatem. And since some Starostas and leaseholders of Our estates are accustomed to exceed the measure in the defence of the estates: We therefore declare the prior statutes made in this matter as follows — that defence is not to be understood as the ploughing up of another's labour, namely crops, buildings, and any work that shall have stood for a year without the Starosta's obstruction; but only as the enjoyment of Our estates, or the bringing of an action after the year to the land court. And if a court, Starosta, or leaseholder should do anyone injury or harm beyond this, the forum for that shall be in the land court where those royal estates are situated. And if the leaseholder had no residence in that palatinate
paciorkowski1776/128: or land, then where he has it, execution shall be made on his estates without delay according to the constitution of the year 1562. And where he has no residence in the Crown, proceedings shall be taken against him according to the procedure agreed at this Sejm against those without possessions; and if he has a sum inscribed in the leasehold, the legal process and execution shall be extended to that sum. And Starostas and leaseholders shall be free to summon anyone before the land court for injuries and losses that occur on the royal plot, both in Our benefit and that of the Commonwealth and in their own; and where oaths are prescribed for them by law, they are to discharge them both in Our name and in their own, saving the appeal to the Tribunal, where such cases are to be determined without remission of the cause. The subjects of Our villages too shall be able to summon before the land court for their own injuries cum assistentia Capitaneorum vel Tenutariorum. Likewise those from Our towns without assistance, according to custom. And where boundaries do not exist, the judges shall be required to send out a commission and conclude the boundaries for the nobleman without interruption. If also, after a commissarial delimitation, a nobleman should take away royal land beyond the boundaries, and be summoned for it before the land court: the court itself shall be required to go out, or to send sworn boundary officials with the court messenger to that plot; and ex re oculis subjecta, at the next sitting shall make a decree, and
paciorkowski1776/129:
shall order the reimbursement of losses according to the liquidation of the injured party by oath.

Provision for boundary commissions.

^[Constitution 1598, fol. 1456, vol. 2.] Inclining ourselves to the ancient laws, We annul all summonses to the Sejm or to the court, issued against the commissioners and the party for the delimitation of all Our estates of whatever kind from terrestrial estates, issued by leaseholders or by Our Instigator; declaring that a commissarial act, conducted by the full number of commissioners according to the laws, is not to be called into any doubt nor impugned, according to the ancient law.

On the manner of delimiting the estates of the inhabitants of Prussia with their adjacent ones.

^[Constitution 1601, fol. 1507, vol. 2.] Since there has not been and is not to this day any means by which the estates of the palatinates and lands adjacent to the Prussian lands under Our authority might be delimited; and the manner of the courts in the palatinates and adjacent lands differs from the courts of the palatinates and lands of Prussia, and in Prussia the Sub-Chamberlains have no jurisdiction in boundary laws — therefore, providing that difficulties from this quarter may not grow on both sides: We enact by the resolution of the present Sejm with the consent of all the estates, that where such differences arise, or
paciorkowski1776/130:
shall arise, without summoning one another before the land courts, the parties, or the party that needs delimitation, may immediately summon to the field; and from one side — that is, from the palatinates and adjacent lands — a Sub-Chamberlain; and from the other side, from Prussia, a land judge or a certain assessor — since they conduct boundaries in Prussia — shall be brought out. Before these, the parties shall appear in secundo termino tanquam peremptorio and dispute the right of path; and to whomever it shall be ordered to lead the boundaries and to swear them according to law, the appeal from their sentence, or where they should disagree, from their divergence, shall be left open to the Tribunal, the prosecution of which shall be directed to that same court among the cases of that land or the other, when they shall be adjudicated at the Tribunal — and in particular that land from which the plaintiff making the summons shall be; and if the plaintiffs are joint, then from that one from which they first lodge the summons. And this is to be understood with respect to the delimitation of hereditary estates and of the estates of Our Table.

Declaration on the boundary commissions of Prussia.

^[Constitution 1613, fol. 185, vol. 3.] Since the inhabitants of Prussia have complained before Us through their deputies that in boundary cases, between Our royal estates and hereditary noble estates, they have not only great difficulty and burden, but must bear delays and arrears
paciorkowski1776/131:
not without futile expense — and this because in even the smallest cases the commissioners admit appeals, and therefore they asked Us to grant them some relief in this matter — We therefore, so that they may know Our favour in this matter too, permit that the lord commissioners may adjudicate and settle small differences that do not exceed two Chełmno włókas without appeal. However, where the difference exceeds the said number of włókas, as the measurement of sworn surveyors shall show — in such cases an appeal from the final sentence to Us shall be permitted. [T.N. 1]

On boundary commissions and commissioners of the Palatinates of Kiev and Bracław.

^[Constitution 1613, fol. 172, vol. 3.] Since on account of the great danger and frequent enemy alarms, the small number of senators, and the vast remoteness of the Palatinates of Kiev and Bracław — when a delimitation of noble estates from Our estates occurs, a nobleman can in no way bring a senator to the commission; whereby the injured person can never obtain justice and delimitation — therefore, providing against this, at the petition of the land deputies of those palatinates, We enact and will: that a senator together with the Sub-Chamberlain and other land officials
paciorkowski1776/132:
specified in the commission, having subscribed himself for the conduct of the commission, shall be required to appear under a fine of ten thousand marks on the senator, for which We preserve the forum for the injured party before the Tribunal. These commissioners, however, appointed by Us, are to conduct themselves according to the constitution of the year 1588 made concerning commissions.

On reviews.

^[Constitution 1647, fol. 125, vol. 4.] Since complaints reach Us from the land deputies that leaseholders of Our estates are conducting reviews inter Bona ab utrinque Nostra cum præjudicio fundi Terrestris per Commissionem antea non dislimitati — We therefore, inclining ourselves to the ancient law concerning commissions made for the delimitation of Our estates with terrestrial ones, declare that Our estates are to be delimited from terrestrial ones by commissioners alone and not by reviewers; without prejudice as between Our estates ab utrinque, which have been and are to be in the future conducted by Our secretaries and not by commissioners. And such reviews, whether conducted in anticipation or after the commission, both before this constitution and in the future, cannot prejudice the terrestrial estate or the commission.
paciorkowski1776/133:
Provision for boundary commissions.

^[Constitution 1651, fol. 712, vol. 4.] Although the security and authority of boundary commissions is sufficiently safeguarded by the common law, there are nevertheless those who, in contravention of the public laws, attempt to invalidate such commissions conducted according to the prescription of the law by various means — by mandates issued to the Sejm and to the court. Therefore, providing against this now and in the future, and reassuming the constitutions of the years 1550, 1567, 1588, 1598, and all other statutes and constitutions on the authority of commissions, by the authority of the present Sejm: We provide that every person who should wish to invalidate such legitimately conducted commissions, whether by mandates or by other means, shall be punished by a fine of five thousand marks, to be recovered before the Crown Tribunal inter causas Officij peremptorie.

Reassumption of the constitutions on commissions.

^[Constitution 1703, fol. 111, vol. 6.] Reassuming the prior constitutions concerning commissions, all commissions and decrees issued by them conducted to this day between Our estates and terrestrial ones, according to the statutes and ancient laws, We preserve inviolably and confirm. Which constitution is also to serve the Grand Duchy of Lithuania
paciorkowski1776/134:
with respect to the delimitation of Our Table estates and terrestrial estates situated in the Crown and in the Grand Duchy of Lithuania.
